what_its_for: Memantine is used to treat moderate to severe Alzheimer's disease. It helps improve memory, thinking, and daily functioning by blocking certain brain signals that can damage brain cells. It does not cure Alzheimer's disease, but it can help slow down some of the symptoms.
how_to_take: Take memantine exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take it with or without food. If you are taking the regular tablets, swallow them whole with a full glass of water. If you are taking the extended-release capsules (Namenda XR), swallow them whole — do not crush, chew, or split them. If you have trouble swallowing the capsule, you may carefully open it and sprinkle the contents onto a small amount of applesauce, then swallow it right away without chewing. The oral solution (liquid form) comes with a special dosing syringe — use only that syringe to measure your dose, not a household spoon.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks to reduce side effects. The typical starting dose is 5 mg once daily. Your doctor will likely increase your dose by 5 mg each week until you reach the target dose of 20 mg per day. For the extended-release capsule, the usual target dose is 28 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once or double up to make up for a missed dose. If you miss several doses in a row, call your doctor or pharmacist before restarting.
storage: Store memantine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. If you have liquid memantine, do not refrigerate or freeze it. Check the label for any specific storage instructions.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other products that contain memantine at the same time, as this can lead to too much medication in your body. Tell your doctor about all other medications, vitamins, and supplements you take. Avoid alcohol while taking memantine, as it may increase dizziness or drowsiness. Be careful with activities that require alertness, such as driving or using machinery, especially when you first start the medication or when your dose is increased, until you know how the medicine affects you.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: severe dizziness, confusion that is worse than usual, hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), unusual changes in mood or behavior, difficulty breathing, seizures, fainting, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you develop any new or worsening symptoms, or if you feel the medication is not helping.
when_it_works: Memantine does not work overnight. It may take several weeks before you or your caregivers notice any improvement in symptoms. Some people notice small improvements in memory, daily activities, or behavior within 4 to 8 weeks. It is important to keep taking the medication every day even if you do not notice immediate changes. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults: Memantine is specifically designed for use in older adults with Alzheimer's disease, but older patients may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, so use extra caution to prevent falls. Kidney problems: If you have kidney disease, your doctor may prescribe a lower dose. Make sure your doctor knows about any kidney problems before you start this medication. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Memantine is not typically used during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor if this applies to you. Children: Memantine is not approved for use in children.
